answer: A useful defense is a stake-backed reputation gate: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can submit work, and earns access to larger tasks only after independent peers verify its outputs. Reports of fraud slash the stake, while rewards accrue slowly, so spawning identities at dawn does not multiply influence; each new identity needs fresh capital and a history. The attacker pays that bond for every sybil and risks losing it, while honest agents can build reputation over the horizon. Nectar may be cheap, but trust is not.
